To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity analysis of Markov networks is as effective as that of Bayesian networks, that the sensitivity analysis is based on the same principles as in Bayesian networks, but the quantification of parameter changes is different.

(1) the same computational methods can be applied in both cases, (2) the same functional form of the conditional probabilities is responsible for this, and (3) the way in which changes in parameters are quantified should be different.

the sensitivity of Markov networks to parameter perturbations can be computed efficiently, and that such sensitivity is more sensitive to changes in the parameters than the sensitivity of Bayesian networks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of Markov networks, we have obtained the same results that were obtained for Bayesian networks, but in the case of Bayesian networks, we have not yet obtained the same results as for Markov networks.

we have shown that Markov networks can be used for the same purposes as Bayesian networks, but that they are not as flexible in their interpretation of parameters, and thus are not suitable for the same applications.

sensitivity analysis for Markov networks is as effective and computationally efficient as sensitivity analysis for Bayesian networks, and that the main difference between these two cases is in the interpretation of the parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sensitivity analysis in Bayesian and Markov network is computationally very similar, and that sensitivity analysis can be applied to Markov networks to improve their performance.
, even though Markov networks and Bayesian networks induce different distributions, they are computationally equivalent for the purposes of sensitivity analysis.
the sensitivity analysis methods developed for Bayesian networks can be applied to Markov networks with little modification.
